title_candidates: ChatGPT Search is leaning harder on site-specific lookups
A simple way to steer ChatGPT Search toward trusted sites
summary: New tracking suggests ChatGPT Search is using far more site-specific web queries. A ten-minute comparison shows how to request and verify a trusted source.

primary_source.title: ChatGPT search now uses the site:operator at scale
primary_source.author: Simon Willison
key_facts: Promptwatch monitors automated prompts across several consumer AI products, and Simon Willison says its aggregate reports can reveal otherwise hidden product changes.
Within Promptwatch's tracked ChatGPT Search sample, the share of background queries limited to a specific site rose from 0.37% on August 7 to 16.8% on August 8.
The same report says average background searches per response rose from about 1.08 to 1.83 that day, consistent with site-specific searches being added alongside broader searches.
Willison cautions that the figures cover only prompts included in Promptwatch's automated tracking, not every ChatGPT search.
Willison could not confirm the internal mechanism and suspects a domain-filter parameter may produce the observed site-restricted queries.

quote_candidates.text: It's important to note that these figures only reflect the prompts for which they have automated tracking enabled.
quote_candidates.position: Paragraph after the first Promptwatch excerpt

supporting_sources.title: ChatGPT Search Now Uses the site:operator at Scale
key_facts: Promptwatch reports a jump from 0.37% to 16.8% in site-restricted fanout queries on August 8 within its tracked sample.
It reports average fanout queries per response rising from about 1.08 to 1.83 at the same time.
Promptwatch describes the trends as aggregated measurements from monitored AI-product interfaces.

supporting_sources.title: Searching the web with ChatGPT
key_facts: OpenAI documents how to select Search from the tools menu or slash menu.
OpenAI tells users to open citations or Sources and check that a page supports the answer.
OpenAI warns that search results and citations can be incomplete, outdated, or incorrect.
Search prompts may be rewritten into targeted queries and sent to search providers.

supporting_sources.title: Freeze, group, hide, or merge rows and columns
key_facts: Google's official Sheets help page gives the expected menu path for freezing a row, making it a harmless citation-check target.

prerequisites: Access to ChatGPT Search in a browser
No private, confidential, or location-sensitive information

steps.instruction: Open ChatGPT, start a new conversation, choose View all tools and Search, and stop if Search is unavailable.
Ask how to freeze the top row in Google Sheets, require web search and citations, then record which domains appear under Sources.
Repeat in a new chat while asking ChatGPT to search only site:support.google.com, then check whether every cited result uses that domain.
Compare the two source lists and mark the restriction unsuccessful if unrelated domains still appear.
Open the Google citation and confirm the page itself supports the menu steps before acting; stop if it does not.
